answer: One strong defense is a bonded stake: to join, an agent locks a deposit in the protocol kernel, like a ship paying to dock at a wharf — creating many fake identities then costs real capital each time. Honest work earns the stake back with rewards, while detected cheating burns it. A comet of cheap fake accounts burns out fast because each identity must pay the same entry price, so the attacker cost scales linearly while the network keeps only identities that keep proving useful work.
